subject: Science
concept: States of Matter: Solid, Liquid, and Gas
standard_explanation: Matter exists in three primary physical states determined by intermolecular forces and thermal kinetic energy. Solids maintain a fixed volume and rigid shape because constituent particles are tightly packed. Liquids possess a definite volume but conform to container shapes as particles slide past one another. Gases have neither fixed shape nor volume, expanding freely as high-energy particles move rapidly.
simplified_explanation: Everything around us is matter! Ice is a solid—it is hard and holds its shape. When ice warms up, it melts into water, which is a liquid you can pour. When water gets very hot, it bubbles into steam, which is an invisible gas floating in the air!
key_points: Solid: Holds its own shape (like an ice cube, pencil, or rock).
Liquid: Flows and takes the shape of its cup (like water, milk, or juice).
Gas: Floats freely all around us (like air, steam, or helium in a balloon).
Heat can change a solid into a liquid, and a liquid into a gas.
examples: An ice pop straight from the freezer is a solid.
Melting ice pop dripping on your hand becomes a liquid.
Steam rising from hot soup into the air is a gas.
misconceptions: Misconception: Gases are not real matter because you often cannot see them. Fact: Air is real gas matter with mass that fills balloons.
Misconception: When ice melts, the water disappears. Fact: The solid ice simply changes state into liquid water.

visual_scenes.title: Solid Ice Cube
visual_scenes.description: A crisp, shiny blue ice cube sits firmly on a plate, keeping its solid box shape.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 1: Solid! Ice is hard, cold, and holds its own rigid shape.

visual_scenes.title: Liquid Melting Water
visual_scenes.description: Warm sunlight melts the ice cube into clear blue liquid that flows across the plate.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 2: Liquid! Warmth melts ice into water that pours and splashes freely.

visual_scenes.title: Gas Rising Steam
visual_scenes.description: Water heats in a pot and turns into light, dancing steam vapors rising into the air.
visual_scenes.caption: Step 3: Gas! Heated water turns into steam that floats freely into the air.

sign_glossary.description: Dominant bent knuckles tap firmly twice against palm of non-dominant hand.
W-handshape index, middle, ring fingers tap gently against bottom lip twice.
Both hands flutter wiggle fingers upward into the air showing rising gas.

assessment_questions.concept: States of Matter: Solid, Liquid, and Gas
assessment_questions.question: What happens to a solid ice cube when it gets warm?
assessment_questions.hint: Think about what happens to an ice cube left out on a warm day.

assessment_questions.concept: States of Matter: Solid, Liquid, and Gas
assessment_questions.question: Which state of matter floats freely all around us in the air?
assessment_questions.hint: We breathe it in with every breath.
